messages.author: cb1a292793a52332
messages.subject: Lines and points does not seem to work…
parts:
Hi all,

I am working on a dataframe with 3 categories (factors) and one variable (numeric)

I use the following code

pl <- ggplot(result,aes(x=P,y=ddo))
pl2 <- pl + geom_hline(yintercept=0) + geom_point(aes(colour=J)) + geom_line(aes(colour=J))
pl2 <- pl2 + facet_wrap(~B) + coord_flip()
pl2 <- pl2 + xlab('Sampling site') + ylab('Phage community performance') + labs(shape='Sampling day')

and get the following output

 

Instead of what I (naively?) expected : the points within each level of "J" should be joined by lines. What did I do wrong?

Cheers,
t

messages.subject: RE: Lines and points does not seem to work.
parts:
Dear Timothée,
 
Is P a categorical variable? In that case geom_line() will not display lines from one category to the next. Probabiliy because lines incase a slope and a slope between categorical levels is non sense. And Hadley tries to prevent that you make non-sense plots with ggplot2.
 
Best regards,
 
Thierry

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Lines and points does not seem to work.
parts:
By default ggplot2 groups observations into geoms by the combination of all categorical variables in the plot.  This doesn't work for lines when you have categorical variables on the x axis, so you need to manually specify the group aesthetic.  Try group = 1.

Hadley

2010/8/12 Timothée Poisot <tpo...@um2.fr>

Dear Thierry,

Yes, P is categorical. I do not agree with the fact that lines joining categorical data are a non-sense, they are actually quite commonly used in ecology/evolution. What if you consider you timepoints to be categorical data, for example?

Are we sure that ggplot2 strictly forbid us to do it?

I added (faked) data to this email. If anyone has some time to play around, that would be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: 539623a2f30c9e53
messages.subject: Re: Lines and points does not seem to work…
parts:
Brandon and Timothy,

Unless otherwise specified, ggplot2 groups by all of the included categorical variables. In this case, it's grouping by J and P (and faceting by B), so each group ends up being only one point, and no lines are drawn. Specifying that it should group only by J solves the problem and gives the intended plot; for comparison, telling it to group only by P would give you vertical lines at each level.

Jonathan
